observation_summary: The HashCodeBuilder uses a ThreadLocal registry to track objects during reflection-based hashCode calculation to prevent infinite recursion in cyclic object graphs. The registry was not being properly cleaned up, leading to memory leaks in container environments and incorrect state (non-null registry) after execution.
hypothesis: The implementation of the ThreadLocal registry was flawed because it initialized the set eagerly and lacked a mechanism to remove the ThreadLocal entry when the registry became empty, causing persistent references and memory leaks.
prediction: The code will be modified to lazily initialize the registry, add null checks when accessing it, and explicitly remove the ThreadLocal entry when the registry is empty to ensure proper cleanup.
experiment_rationale: The fix diff shows the removal of the initialValue() override in the ThreadLocal definition, the addition of null checks in isRegistered, and the addition of logic in register and unregister to manage the lifecycle of the ThreadLocal entry (creating it on demand and removing it when empty). This confirms the issue was the lifecycle management of the registry.
reasoning_summary: The defect is an algorithmic/procedural issue regarding the lifecycle management of a shared resource (the ThreadLocal registry). The fix involves changing the initialization strategy (lazy vs eager) and adding logic to clean up the resource when no longer needed. This is a procedural correction to how the registry is maintained, fitting the Algorithm/Method category.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the initialization strategy changed from eager to lazy, the core issue is the procedural logic for managing the lifecycle of the ThreadLocal entry, which is more complex than a simple value assignment.
While null checks were added, they are part of the broader procedural fix to manage the lifecycle of the registry, not just a missing guard.
